structured_output.summary: The change implements Atomics.isLockFree in the spec's order. ToIntegerOrInfinity(size) is called first with `?` propagation. The branches for n = 1, 2, 4 and 8 and the final `false` follow the spec's conditions exactly. Nothing is keyed on test-specific inputs, no errors are swallowed, and there are no unrelated edits. The only judgment call is the three constants IS_LOCK_FREE_1, _2 and _8, all set to true. The spec leaves [[IsLockFree1/2/8]] implementation-defined and the engine has no Agent Record for them, so a documented per-file constant is a defensible choice. It is not a guess presented as a computed result. The value should still be checked against the real atomic implementation.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: The change is acceptable as is. Two follow-ups for the architect, neither blocking. (1) IS_LOCK_FREE_1, IS_LOCK_FREE_2 and IS_LOCK_FREE_8 in crates/kahvi-builtins/src/atomics/is_lock_free.rs are hardcoded to true. Confirm that the engine's atomic operations on 1-, 2- and 8-byte elements really take no lock. If an Agent Record with [[IsLockFree*]] fields is added later, read the values from it instead of these constants. (2) The spec NOTE block was dropped from the source comments. That is not an algorithm step, so it is not a spec violation, but restore it if the house style requires all spec text to stay in place.
